sentences.text: Party No.2 has alleged that co-accused Durga Prasad Gupta was awarded a work by M/s Assam Coal Products Limited who had sought financial assistance of Rs.7,22,000/- from Bank of India in respect of which the informant had agreed to stand as a guarantor by way of signing on Bank guarantee form in good faith, but no money was disbursed in which he stood as guarantor.

It is further stated that Bank of India had earlier sanctioned Rs.6,30,000/- in the name of Larkco Engineering to co-accused Durga Prasad Gupta and as such, he received Rs.3,00,000/- out of Rs.6,30,000/- for which Swaraj Kumar Nandi and Dr. Prasad stood as guarantors.

It is further stated by the informant that co-accused Durga Prasad Gupta with the help of the petitioner utilized his bank guarantee papers in several location and fraudulently inserted his name as previous guarantor for the sanction of Rs.3,00,000/- which the informant has got no knowledge.

It is further stated by the informant that Bank of India had filed a case against him and had got decree by committing impersonation as somebody else signed Vakalatnama and affidavit forging his signature.

5. Mr. Das, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that the petitioner was posted as Branch Manager of Bhulan Bararee Branch of Bank of India for the period from June, 1990 to July 1992.
He submits that in the complaint petition the date of occurrence is shown as 2007 till today and the complaint case was filed on 29.09.2011.
He further submits that in the complaint petition itself, O.P. No. 2 has stated that the Bank has obtained a decree for recovery of the loan in question from the DRT.

He further submits that the informant / complainant himself has admitted that his guarantee paper was utilized for the loan amount sanctioned much earlier to Larkco Engineering of co-accused Durga Prasad Gupta.

He further submits that the petitioner has served for the Bank of India at Dhanbad since 15.09.1988 to 31.12.1993 and since 01.01.1994, he was posted at Kolkata region and retired from service in July, 2009 itself.

He submits that if the occurrence is found to be true, the petitioner was not posted in the district of Dhanbad and the entire criminal proceeding has maliciously been instituted against the petitioner.
6. Mr. Srivastava, learned A.P.P. appearing for the state submits that the learned court has rightly taken the cognizance.

7. In view of the above, the court has perused the complaint petition as well as the order taking cognizance and finds that admittedly in the complaint petition, the averments made therein shows that the occurrence has said to be occurred from 2007 to till date of filing the complaint petition i.e.
on 29.09.2011, wherein the petitioner had worked in the district of Dhanbad since 15.09.1988 to 31.12.1993 and thereafter since 01.01.1994, he was posted at Kolkata region and retired from service in July, 2009 itself.
In the complaint petition itself, the O.P. No. 2 has admitted that the Bank has obtained a decree for recovery of the loan in question from the DRT.
Thus, it is crystal clear that the petitioner was not posted during the time of alleged occurrence, as has been disclosed in the complaint.
8. In view of the above facts, reasons and analysis, to allow to continue the proceedings against the petitioner will amount to an abuse of the process of law.

Accordingly, the entire criminal proceedings including the orders dated 15.05.2014, 07.04.2016 and 07.01.2017, by which, warrant of arrest, process under Section 82 Cr.P.C. and cognizance have been taken against the petitioner, in Bernard Basanto D'Rozario vs The State Of Jharkhand on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69473638/
2 connection with Jorapokhar (Sudamdih) P.S. Case No. 49 of 2012 corresponding to G.R. No. 1016 of 2012, pending in the court of learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Dhanbad, are hereby, quashed so far as this petitioner is concerned.
